{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABZkTz1w", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhDK7YY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 93, "title": "Implement 8253 binary mode-4 software-triggered strobe and IRQ delivery", "body": "## Problem

Binary PIT mode 4 is missing. At baseline `065f02bc0840924c62270496d4798882a89940e7`, [Counter::write/tick](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/065f02b/src/devices.rs#L214-L301) immediately replaces the running count and uses periodic toggling for mode 4. [Pit::write](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/065f02b/src/devices.rs#L411-L455) initializes OUT and cancels prior activity only for modes 0/2/3, so selecting mode 4 can retain an earlier countdown, OUT state and latch.

This prevents guest software from obtaining a software-triggered, one-clock strobe with coherent counter readback and IRQ0 delivery. Existing [PIT tests](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/065f02b/tests/pit.rs) cover modes 0/2/3, rewrites and latches, but provide no mode-4 acceptance.

## Expected outcome

Implement binary mode 4 for all three shared counters, under the existing held-high GATE model.

Intel’s [8253/8253-5 datasheet, Mode 4 and Counter Loading](https://www.cpu-galaxy.at/CPU/Ram%20Rom%20Eprom/Other_Intel_chips/other_intel-Dateien/C8253.pdf) defines initial high OUT, a terminal-count low pulse lasting one input clock, and software restart through count programming. Preserve the documented byte formats, independent counters and ordinary count-latch behavior.

Use the [Intel 8254 datasheet, Mode 4/Figure 19](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/23wi-cs212/pintos/specs/8254.pdf#page=15) as supplementary timing clarification for this shared behavior:

- A fresh mode word establishes high OUT immediately and cancels the previous sequence; counting awaits a complete initial value.
- A complete initial or replacement value transfers on the next clock without decrementing. For count N, OUT falls N+1 clocks after the completed write and rises one clock later.
- During a paired replacement, the first byte leaves counting unaffected; the second schedules the next-clock load. A write alone does not force an OUT transition.
- Encoded binary zero represents 65,536. Counting continues through 16-bit wrap after terminal count, while the completed strobe remains high until another software-triggered sequence. See [Figure 22 and Counter semantics](https://www.scs.stanford.edu/23wi-cs212/pintos/specs/8254.pdf#page=17).

Integrate actual rising transitions with existing IRQ0 delivery. For channel 1, use mode-4 OUT for beeper polarity within the current sample scheduler.

Non-goals: external GATE inputs, modes 1/5, BCD, 8254 read-back, unrelated access-sequencing changes, clock-frequency changes, audio-scheduler redesign or electrical fidelity.

## Context and reproduction

The following original reproduction is proposed for the Coordinator to add and execute:

```rust
let mut pit = pc98_rust::devices::Pit::default();
pit.write(3, 0x36); // known high OUT
pit.write(3, 0x38); // channel 0, paired binary mode 4
pit.write(0, 3);
pit.write(0, 0);
assert!(!pit.tick(5)); // exactly one clock at the current scheduler ratio
assert_eq!((pit.c[0].remaining, pit.c[0].output), (3, true));
```

Static inspection predicts baseline count 2 instead of 3 because the load clock is missing. Selecting mode 4 after mode 0 also fails to establish initial high OUT. These are longstanding gaps, separate from PR #92.

Project progress: inspection of the latest device/bus diff supports the reported bounded PIC change: SNGL controls initialization sequencing and local master-IR7 delivery. The [Coordinator’s PR #92 report](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/pull/92) and [validation record](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/065f02b/docs/validation.md#issue-91-8259a-single-mode-initialization-and-delivery-2026-10-24) report 363 native and 130 production release-Wasm browser cases passing. Default browser startup ran zero cases because of an occupied port; the reported alternate-port run retained both hosting roots and existing assertions/budgets. No independent review or remote CI result was supplied. This evaluator executed no builds/tests and prepared no fixtures.

All 26 inventory categories and their fixed scopes remain unchanged: 24 partial, GRCG implemented_unverified, paging unimplemented; none verified. The supplied open-Issue list is empty, and supplied completed improvements do not include mode 4.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record the original reproduction failing on the baseline and passing after implementation. Add original `mode4_` Rust tests with literal specification-derived expectations, independent of production counter logic.
- [ ] Verify initialization from active modes 0/2/3 and mode 4, including prior low OUT, pending loads, incomplete writes and unread latches. Fresh programming cancels stale state without disturbing other channels. Do not assert an undefined pre-load count.
- [ ] Verify all channels and LSB-only, MSB-only and paired formats, including counts 1, 2, 3, FFFFh and encoded zero where representable. For N=3, require successive clock states `(count, OUT, rise)` of `(3,H,0), (2,H,0), (1,H,0), (0,L,0), (FFFFh,H,1), (FFFEh,H,0)`. Channel-0 tick reporting alone exposes the rise.
- [ ] Cover count-only replacement before loading, during countdown, across terminal count and during/after the low strobe. Include delayed paired completion, latest complete value before a load, and an unfinished following pair. Preserve any old strobe reached before replacement completion; retain ordinary latch snapshots until their programmed read completes. Verify continued count readback across multiple wraps without periodic output or IRQ recurrence.
- [ ] Compare single-clock execution, irregular batches and large scheduler advances, including `tick(0)`, fractional clocks and `u32::MAX`. Final counter state and accumulated rising-edge indication must agree; a batch crossing the complete low pulse must retain its rise. Avoid per-clock iteration for large elapsed intervals.
- [ ] On VM and Ap, exercise both port banks and cross-bank accesses. Distinguish a programming-induced low-to-high setup edge from the strobe edge. After draining setup requests, require no IRQ on the falling edge and exactly one strobe IRQ, with mask/IRR retention, ISR/normal EOI, IF deferral and real handler/IRET behavior. Channels 1/2 must not generate IRQ0. Check isolation and reset during partial-write, pending-load, countdown, low-pulse and completed phases.
- [ ] Add focused channel-1 checks showing mode-4 beeper polarity follows OUT at sample endpoints, including after counter wrap. Preserve existing mode-3 audio behavior; disclose the retained batched-sampling limitation.
- [ ] Add an original MIT assembly boot probe, offline preparation helper and checked provenance/hash manifest, following existing PIT fixture conventions. Through guest I/O, exercise both port banks, software replacement and repeated arming, natural IRQ0 handlers/EOI/IRET, advancing post-terminal latched counts and a quiet interval exceeding one full wrap. Hosts only mount, step, inspect and reset. Require exact independent result bytes/guards, `PIT MODE4 PASS` without `FAIL`, unchanged media and no errors within 2,000,000 scheduler slots per boot.
- [ ] Boot the identical probe natively and in production release-Wasm on VM/Ap, cold and after reset, at `/` and `/pc98-rust/`. Browser checks also reject page/console errors. Integrate preparation into README/CI; keep generated fixtures outside the publication tree. No commercial ROMs or guest-software acquisition is required for this probe.
- [ ] The Coordinator runs README prerequisites, `python3 tools/prepare_pit_mode4_fixture.py`, `cargo test --locked --test pit mode4_`, `cargo test --locked`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`, `git diff --check` and `npm test`. Preserve existing PIT/PIC/BIOS timer, CPU interrupt-shadow, audio, DOS/apps, VM and six-game assertions and budgets. Report exact outcomes and any equivalent browser-port substitution.
- [ ] Update hardware/validation documentation with implemented semantics, source links and actual pre-merge evidence. PIT remains partial: modes 1/5, external GATE/retriggering, BCD, remaining access/latch sequencing, mode-2/3 divisor-1 behavior and fuller beeper timing remain outstanding. Protected execution, paging, numerical x87 and every other inventory gap remain required. Limited probes establish neither full hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Optional validation

None.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
